message: Hardcoded rate limit bypass: request origin header is trusted without validation, allowing clients to spoof IP addresses and circumvent rate limiting
recommendation: Validate and sanitize the X-Forwarded-For header or use a trusted proxy configuration (e.g. Express `trust proxy` setting). Never trust client-supplied headers for rate limit key derivation without verification.

message: Missing authentication check on proxy forwarding — any unauthenticated request can be forwarded to internal services, bypassing the API gateway auth layer
evidence: router.post('/proxy/:service', async (req, res) => { await forwardRequest(req, res); });
recommendation: Apply the authentication middleware before the proxy handler. Add `requireAuth` middleware to the route: `router.post('/proxy/:service', requireAuth, async (req, res) => { ... })`

message: Upstream response body is not size-limited before being buffered into memory — a large downstream response can exhaust heap and crash the process
recommendation: Stream the upstream response directly to the client using `response.body.pipe(res)`, or enforce a max body size limit before buffering. Consider using `got` with `responseType: 'buffer'` and a size limit.

message: JWT verification error is silently swallowed and treated as unauthenticated; attacker can probe token structure without any log evidence
recommendation: Log the error at warn level with sanitized context (never the token itself) before calling `next()` with an authentication error. Distinguishing expired vs. malformed vs. invalid-signature errors aids incident response.

message: Route lookup iterates all registered routes on every request with O(n) linear scan — should use a radix tree or pre-compiled lookup map
recommendation: Replace linear scan with a trie/radix-tree router (e.g. `find-my-way`) or pre-compile route patterns into a lookup map keyed by path prefix at startup time.

message: Token bucket refill logic has no unit tests — edge cases like concurrent refill and burst exhaustion are untested
recommendation: Add unit tests covering: (1) bucket refills to capacity but not beyond, (2) concurrent requests from the same client don't over-consume tokens, (3) burst limit is enforced after initial fill.

message: console.log used instead of structured logger — log lines are unparseable by log aggregation tools
recommendation: Replace with the project's pino logger: `import { logger } from '@prguardian/observability'; logger.info({ ...context }, message);`

message: Validation schema imported but never applied to the request body — schema is dead code and request shape is unchecked
evidence: import { requestSchema } from '../schemas/request.js'; // schema defined but validate() never called
recommendation: Call `requestSchema.parse(req.body)` and handle the resulting ZodError, or remove the unused import if validation is intentionally deferred.

message: Config module exports a mutable object — callers can accidentally mutate shared config values at runtime
recommendation: Freeze the config object with `Object.freeze()` or use `as const` assertion to make all properties readonly at the TypeScript type level.

message: Health check handler has no test — a future refactor could silently break the /healthz endpoint
recommendation: Add a smoke test: `it('GET /healthz returns 200', async () => { const res = await request(app).get('/healthz'); expect(res.status).toBe(200); });`
